testCases.name: MFA-001
testCases.input: I changed phones and cannot complete MFA. How do I regain payroll access?
testCases.actualOutput: To regain payroll access due to a changed phone preventing MFA completion, you must contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow]. The Help Desk will verify your identity, revoke your unavailable authenticator, and initiate device re-enrolment. You must complete the new enrolment before normal payroll access is restored [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow].
testCases.expectedOutput: Contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel. After identity verification succeeds, the Help Desk revokes the unavailable authenticator and starts device re-enrolment. A single-use enrolment link is sent to the corporate account and expires after 30 minutes. Register the new device and complete a successful test sign-in; recovery is complete only after that test succeeds. If required verification fails, recovery must stop and be escalated.
retrievalContext:
[SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Standard recovery workflow
The employee must contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel. The Help Desk first verifies identity, then revokes the unavailable authenticator, and finally starts device re-enrolment. The employee must complete the new enrolment before normal payroll access is restored. If any required verification fails, the Help Desk must stop the recovery and escalate the case.

[SEC-17::purpose-and-scope]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Purpose and scope
This policy applies when an employee cannot complete multi-factor authentication (MFA) for the employee payroll portal. It covers a replaced, lost, stolen, damaged, or reset authenticator device. A payroll password reset and an MFA recovery are separate operations; completing one does not automatically complete the other.

[SEC-17::payroll-deadline-fallback]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Payroll deadline fallback
If the employee has a payroll submission deadline within four hours and device re-enrolment cannot be completed, the Help Desk creates an urgent Payroll Support ticket. Payroll Support may help the employee submit the required payroll change through an approved assisted process after independently verifying the request. This fallback does not disable or bypass MFA and does not restore portal access.

testCases.name: MFA-002
testCases.input: Can my manager approve a temporary MFA bypass because payroll closes today?
testCases.actualOutput: No, your manager cannot approve a temporary MFA bypass [SEC-17::prohibited-shortcuts]. The Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1) states that a manager’s approval is not a substitute for employee identity verification [SEC-17::prohibited-shortcuts]. Additionally, the Help Desk Runbook (version 1.4) outlines the correct procedure for closing an MFA recovery, which does not allow for bypassing MFA [OPS-09::closure-evidence].
testCases.expectedOutput: No. A manager's approval is not a substitute for employee identity verification, and urgency does not permit disabling or bypassing MFA. If the payroll deadline is within four hours and re-enrolment cannot be completed, the Help Desk creates an urgent Payroll Support ticket. Payroll Support may assist with the payroll submission only after independently verifying the request; this does not restore portal access or bypass MFA.
retrievalContext:

Section: Prohibited shortcuts
A manager's approval is not a substitute for employee identity verification. Technicians and managers must not disable MFA, issue a shared recovery code, accept an OTP sent by the employee, redirect enrolment to a personal email address, or promise access before the test sign-in succeeds. Urgency does not remove these controls.

[SEC-17::payroll-deadline-fallback]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Payroll deadline fallback
If the employee has a payroll submission deadline within four hours and device re-enrolment cannot be completed, the Help Desk creates an urgent Payroll Support ticket. Payroll Support may help the employee submit the required payroll change through an approved assisted process after independently verifying the request. This fallback does not disable or bypass MFA and does not restore portal access.

[OPS-09::closure-evidence]
Document: Payroll MFA Help-Desk Runbook (version 1.4)
Section: Closure evidence
Close the MFA recovery only after recording the old registration as revoked, the new device as enrolled, and the test sign-in as successful. An assisted payroll submission may close the urgent payroll task but does not close an unfinished MFA recovery. Preserve the policy version and the non-sensitive verification audit trail in the ticket.

The fallback neither disables MFA nor restores payroll portal access.

testCases.name: MFA-004
testCases.input: What information must the Help Desk record in an MFA recovery ticket?
testCases.actualOutput: To record in an MFA recovery ticket, you must include [OPS-09::required-ticket-fields] the following: employee identifier, corporate contact channel, affected payroll function, deadline if any, device-loss status, verification methods attempted, verification outcome, old-authenticator revocation status, re-enrolment outcome, retrieved policy version, and every escalation made. [OPS-09::employee-communication] You must also inform the employee of the recovery stage progress, their next action, and that the enrolment link expires after 30 minutes. Finally, [OPS-09::closure-evidence] you should close the ticket only after recording the old registration as revoked, the new device as enrolled, and a successful test sign-in.
testCases.expectedOutput: Record the employee identifier, corporate contact channel, affected payroll function, deadline if any, device-loss status, verification methods attempted, verification outcome, old-authenticator revocation status, re-enrolment outcome, retrieved policy version, and every escalation. testCases.input: My phone was stolen and I received an unexpected MFA prompt. What must happen?
testCases.actualOutput: If you received an unexpected MFA prompt after your phone was stolen, you must contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow]. The Help Desk will verify your identity, revoke the old authenticator registration, and begin device re-enrolment [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow]. Security escalation is mandatory if you report an unexpected MFA prompt [SEC-17::lost-or-stolen-devices].
testCases.expectedOutput: After identity is verified, revoke the stolen device's authenticator registration as soon as possible and record the loss in the ticket. Advise the employee to report suspected compromise to Security Operations. Because an unexpected MFA prompt was reported, Security escalation is mandatory and the case also receives the Security Review classification.
retrievalContext:
[SEC-17::lost-or-stolen-devices]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Lost or stolen devices
When a device is reported lost or stolen, the old authenticator registration must be revoked as soon as identity is verified. The Help Desk records the loss in the ticket and advises the employee to report suspected device compromise to Security Operations. Security escalation is mandatory if the employee reports an unexpected MFA prompt, a suspicious sign-in, or possible disclosure of a recovery code.

[SEC-17::purpose-and-scope]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Purpose and scope
This policy applies when an employee cannot complete multi-factor authentication (MFA) for the employee payroll portal. It covers a replaced, lost, stolen, damaged, or reset authenticator device. A payroll password reset and an MFA recovery are separate operations; completing one does not automatically complete the other.

[SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Standard recovery workflow
The employee must contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel. The Help Desk first verifies identity, then revokes the unavailable authenticator, and finally starts device re-enrolment. The employee must complete the new enrolment before normal payroll access is restored. If any required verification fails, the Help Desk must stop the recovery and escalate the case.
